proposed_widenings.name: shared_resource_pool_across_composite_parts
proposed_widenings.justification: Channel Divinity is one class feature with one shared use-count pool. Both Divine Spark and Turn Undead draw from the same pool of uses. CompositeClassFeatureMechanics exists but each ActivatedAbilityMechanics part carries its own independent resource — there is no mechanism to declare that multiple activation options share a single named pool. This is the defining structural characteristic of Channel Divinity (and analogous class features like Bardic Inspiration sub-options, Monk Ki).
proposed_widenings.evidence: You can use this class's Channel Divinity twice. You regain one of its expended uses when you finish a Short Rest, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest. [...] Each time you use this class's Channel Divinity, choose which Channel Divinity effect from this class to create.

proposed_widenings.name: activation_time_choice_between_heal_and_save_gate
proposed_widenings.justification: Divine Spark requires an activation-time choice between (a) applying heal_hp directly or (b) opening a save_gate resolution that applies damage on fail / half-damage on success. CastTimeEffectModeChoice exists but only accepts ReadonlyNonEmptyArray<EffectAtom> per option — save_gate is an ActivationPhase kind, not an EffectAtom. There is no mechanism to have a mode choice where one branch is a bare EffectAtom and another branch is a resolution phase. A new conditional-branch activation-phase shape (or widening of CastTimeEffectModeChoice to accept ActivationPhase-typed options) is required.
proposed_widenings.evidence: Roll 1d8 and add your Wisdom modifier. You either restore Hit Points to the creature equal to that total or force the creature to make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the creature takes Necrotic or Radiant damage (your choice) equal to that total. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage (round down).

proposed_widenings.name: DurationEndTrigger.caster_has_condition / caster_dies
proposed_widenings.justification: Turn Undead's duration ends early if the caster gains the Incapacitated condition or dies. DurationEndTrigger has target_takes_damage, target_makes_attack_roll, target_deals_damage, etc., but no caster-state variants. Two new closed variants are needed: { kind: 'caster_has_condition'; condition: Condition } and { kind: 'caster_dies' }.
proposed_widenings.evidence: This effect ends early on the creature if it takes any damage, if you have the Incapacitated condition, or if you die.

notes: Three independent blocking gaps. The dominating issue is (1): the shared resource pool is structurally irrepresentable — you cannot split Channel Divinity into two independent ActivatedAbilityMechanics parts without duplicating and diverging the use pool, which would misrepresent RAW. Gap (2) is also structural: Divine Spark's heal-vs-damage choice requires mode branches where one branch is a resolution-phase (save_gate), not just an EffectAtom. Gap (3) is a surface widening that also blocks Turn Undead's honest encoding. Secondary omission: the damage-type choice in Divine Spark ('Necrotic or Radiant, your choice') maps to CastTimeChoice<DamageType> which already exists, so that part is expressible once the broader gaps are resolved. The 'tries to move away' behavior in Turn Undead is fully implied by the Frightened condition (can't willingly move toward source of fear) and does not require a new atom.
